searchText: Do non-mining nodes in the p2p network store the transactions in the mempool? If so, what's the benefit of storing them, instead of, say, storing the hashes? Do they need to rebroadcast at any point significantly later than the one time they rebroadcast after they first receive and validate the tx? Yes they do store them. Potentially they could only store them for a short period if they're not mining and then just record hashes of transactions they seen. Other nodes may request the full transaction by hash but there's no obligation that a tx advertised by hash is available indefinitely from a node (there's already pruning obviously). If they're only publishing tx hashes then they'd need to store the tx for some period to ensure it propagates well but I'd be surprised if it needed to be for longer than something like 30s and possibly not even that. Right, after a short republishing window it seems like just storing a 32 byte hash (or even 8 byte hash with a private client-side nonce) for anti-duplication purposes should be sufficient... I think the TLDR is that the mempools tend to be small enough that no one really cares to hyper optimize them. Right, I'm thinking about this in the context of account abstraction where mempool costs do end up going up especially in the attack case I'm of the opinion that people shouldn't be using the global mempool for long-term storage of transactions, and with 1559 transactions should flush through the mempool quite quickly, so there isn't really a need for a big one. <@&688090867927482525> it seems you're removing eth/65 in 1.10.8 (https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/23120) is that the plan? I know you've mentioned it a few times on ACD before that it would be gone post-London, but if it is happening in the next release, just want to make sure it's re-shared here so all clients are aware 👍 Yes, it is going to be in the next release when do you expect to cut 1.10.8? 2 wooks? <@&836981603216654336> folks, we need eth/66 support soon We have a draft pr for it but will need to revisit. Rai is on it I think @fjl has a test suite for eth/66 in hive That might help do a rough verification at least Hi all, regarding this PR. https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/251. What is the final decision ? What we want to put on the gasPrice field ? - Unmined gasPrice (for Legacy transaction) maxFeeCapPerGas (for 1559 transaction) - Mined effectivePriorityFeePerGas (for 1559 transaction) gasPrice (for Legacy transaction) <@!543900561460822016> Does dropping eth/65 in geth break any other clients?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: If so, what's the benefit of storing them, instead of, say, storing the hashes?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Do they need to rebroadcast at any point significantly later than the one time they rebroadcast after they first receive and validate the tx?

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: Yes they do store them.  Potentially they could only store them for a short period if they're not mining and then just record hashes of transactions they seen. Other nodes may request the full transaction by hash but there's no obligation that a tx advertised by hash is available indefinitely from a node (there's already pruning obviously). If they're only publishing tx hashes then they'd need to store the tx for some period to ensure it propagates well but I'd be surprised if it needed to be for longer than something like 30s and possibly not even that.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Right, after a short republishing window it seems like just storing a 32 byte hash (or even 8 byte hash with a private client-side nonce) for anti-duplication purposes should be sufficient...

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I think the TLDR is that the mempools tend to be small enough that no one really cares to hyper optimize them.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Right, I'm thinking about this in the context of account abstraction where mempool costs do end up going up especially in the attack case

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I'm of the opinion that people shouldn't be using the global mempool for long-term storage of transactions, and with 1559 transactions should flush through the mempool quite quickly, so there isn't really a need for a big one.
